verdicts.trueWording: That kind of gap is very fertile ground for a novelist

That kind of gap is very fertile ground for a novelist.' Every limb present.

verdicts.trueWording: I like finding corners of history that have been under-explored

verdicts.trueWording: I am drawn as a reader to intelligent characters
verdicts.note: Live fetch, brightweavings.com/patrick (Interview with Patrick St-Denis), answer on extraordinary individuals: 'I am drawn as a reader to intelligent characters, I get irritated if I feel too much smarter than the characters (unless that's being done with purpose, and it can be).' All three limbs present.

verdicts.trueWording: Emotion is often conveyed by what is not said.

verdicts.trueWording: make the world be as my characters believe it to be

verdicts.trueWording: it removes that smugness from the reader
verdicts.note: Live fetch, same LARB answer: 'there's a slightly smug patronizing attitude that kicks in' about the past, and 'The strength of this, for me, is enormous, because it removes that smugness from the reader who's willing to go there.' Both limbs present.

verdicts.trueWording: The two moons say, We're not here
verdicts.note: Live fetch, LARB. Interviewer: 'you're setting the rules of engagement? So your reader knows you're not talking about Justinian himself?' Kay: 'That's right. That's also one of the reasons I've used two moons in several of the books. The two moons say, We're not here.' The 'signal to the reader' limb rests on that exchange.

verdicts.trueWording: if a reader can pick out what's made up and what's real, you've botched your storytelling
verdicts.note: Live fetch, LARB, answer to the question quoting Kay's Bring Up the Bodies (Hilary Mantel) review. Verbatim.

verdicts.trueWording: it's also, for me, staggeringly alien
verdicts.note: Live fetch, LARB, answer to the Aldous Huxley quotation: 'The past is sometimes refreshingly different, but it's also, for me, staggeringly alien. I think it's important for people writing about the past to acknowledge and work with that.' Both limbs present.

verdicts.trueWording: A reverence for language runs through everything he writes.
verdicts.note: Live fetch, LARB, interviewer's introduction ('Kay and I met in Toronto in early June...'), byline Christine Fischer Guy, August 14 2016. Verbatim.

verdicts.trueWording: The approximate number of the dead could also point in the same direction
verdicts.note: Live fetch, brightweavings hosting of Roosa Toyryla's 2017 University of Helsinki bachelor's thesis (page states: 'This is a bachelor's thesis by Roosa Toyryla, written at the University of Helsinki, Finland. 2017.'). Section 'Narratorial Focalization: All-seeing but Indifferent'. Quoted novel passage gives 'some thirty or forty Senzians'; thesis adds 'the exact number of casualties does not seem to be of great importance'. Note: the thesis calls the Senzio incident a 'bloody, to-the-death melee' / slaughter, not a 'massacre' - the claim's own label, not a separate factual limb.

verdicts.trueWording: it strengthens the illusion of there being a world full of other stories
verdicts.note: Live fetch, same thesis, section 'Minor Characters as Focal Characters: Less Important People?': 'The Governor's experience is not essential to the story, but it strengthens the illusion of there being a world full of other stories around the one the novel is about.' Governor of Stevanien named as the focal character earlier in the same section.
